BulkUnitItem.description:
One unit in a bulk creation request.

``complex_name`` and ``suburb`` are deliberately absent: both are taken from
the estate server-side, so a caller cannot label units with a name of their
choosing. Anything extra is rejected outright.
BulkUnitItem.title: BulkUnitItem

BulkUnitsRequest.description: Create many units in one all-or-nothing request (1 to 500).
BulkUnitsRequest.title: BulkUnitsRequest

ComplaintCreate.description:
What a resident or HOA admin files. The category and priority are the
fixed vocabulary, so the contract publishes the allowed values (BE-1).

The response DTOs below deliberately stay plain strings: rows filed before
the vocabulary existed may carry a free-text category, and they must still
read back.
ComplaintCreate.title: ComplaintCreate

EstateAccessListResponse.description: All estates the caller can select. Empty means provisioning is pending.
EstateAccessListResponse.title: EstateAccessListResponse

EstateAccessResponse.description: One estate the authenticated user has a persisted membership in.
EstateAccessResponse.title: EstateAccessResponse

EstatePhotoResponse.description: One photo of the estate, as its administrator manages it.
EstatePhotoResponse.title: EstatePhotoResponse

EstatePhotoUpdate.description: Reorder or re-caption one photo. The image itself is never replaced.
EstatePhotoUpdate.title: EstatePhotoUpdate

EstateProfileResponse.description: The profile an estate's members can read.
EstateProfileResponse.title: EstateProfileResponse

EstateProfileUpdate.description: What an estate administrator may change. The name is not editable.

HealthBriefFeedbackRequest.description: A member's verdict on one stored brief. No extra fields: nothing to smuggle.
HealthBriefFeedbackRequest.title: HealthBriefFeedbackRequest

HealthBriefResponse.description: The estate's brief, with the numbers it was allowed to use.
HealthBriefResponse.title: HealthBriefResponse

IncidentCreate.description:
What an HOA admin may send when recording an incident.

``estate_id``, ``status`` and ``created_by`` are deliberately absent: the
estate comes from an authorized membership, the status always starts at
``open`` and the author is the logged-in admin. Unknown fields are refused
rather than silently dropped.
IncidentCreate.title: IncidentCreate

IncidentResponse.description: One incident. The three admin-only fields are null for other members.
IncidentResponse.title: IncidentResponse

IncidentUpdate.description:
The only patchable fields.

``category``, ``occurred_at``, ``estate_id`` and ``property_id`` are
immutable, and ``status`` moves only along the allowed transitions (the
service owns those). Because unknown fields are refused, an attempt to patch
an immutable field is a 422 rather than a silent no-op.
IncidentUpdate.title: IncidentUpdate

JoinCodeCreateRequest.description:
Rotate the estate's join code.

``expires_in_days`` is optional: an omitted value issues a code that does not
expire until it is rotated. The estate is never part of the body - it is a
query parameter, and the membership check is what proves access.
JoinCodeCreateRequest.title: JoinCodeCreateRequest

JoinCodeResponse.description:
The active code, returned only from an authenticated request body/response.

The code appears here and nowhere else: never in a path, a query string, a log
line or an error message.
JoinCodeResponse.title: JoinCodeResponse

LivingScoreComponentResponse.description: One component of a stored score, exactly as the engine described it.
LivingScoreComponentResponse.title: LivingScoreComponentResponse

LivingScoreHistoryResponse.description: A page of an estate's score history, newest first.
LivingScoreHistoryResponse.title: LivingScoreHistoryResponse

LivingScoreHistoryRow.description:
A summary of one stored snapshot, for the history list.

Deliberately small: the history is a trajectory, so it carries the date, the
status and the number. The full breakdown is one request per snapshot away.
LivingScoreHistoryRow.title: LivingScoreHistoryRow

LivingScoreSnapshotResponse.description: One stored Living Score calculation, with its full breakdown.
LivingScoreSnapshotResponse.title: LivingScoreSnapshotResponse

MembershipJoinRequest.description:
A resident's join request: the shared code plus their unit number.

The code is normalised again inside the service (case, spaces and hyphens are
all tolerated), so this DTO only trims it and enforces a length.
MembershipJoinRequest.title: MembershipJoinRequest

MembershipJoinResponse.description:
The narrow confirmation a resident gets after joining.

Deliberately tiny: the estate they can now act in, the unit the membership is
attached to, and the role. Never the code, never another member, never any
other estate's data.
MembershipJoinResponse.title: MembershipJoinResponse

MembershipProviderAddRequest.description:
An estate admin adding a registered service provider to their estate.

The email is the only input: the estate comes from ``?estate_id=`` and the
provider's own account and profile already exist (they registered
themselves). A ``user_id`` or ``provider_id`` here would let an admin bind
the wrong account.
MembershipProviderAddRequest.title: MembershipProviderAddRequest

MembershipResponse.description: One row of the admin's member list.
MembershipResponse.title: MembershipResponse

PendingResidencyCountResponse.description: The badge number for the admin navigation.
PendingResidencyCountResponse.title: PendingResidencyCountResponse

ProviderSignup.description:
The minimal provider profile created alongside a service_provider account.

The profile's email and full name are the account's, so they are not accepted
here; ``verified`` is always false and only a platform admin may change it.
ProviderSignup.title: ProviderSignup

ProvisionAccountRequest.description: Operator-only account provisioning; clients cannot supply arbitrary roles.
ProvisionAccountRequest.title: ProvisionAccountRequest

PublicEstateDetailResponse.description: The public detail page for one published estate.
PublicEstateDetailResponse.title: PublicEstateDetailResponse

PublicEstateListItem.description: One row of the public grid.
PublicEstateListItem.title: PublicEstateListItem

PublicLivingScoreSummary.description:
Four fields of the latest stored snapshot, and nothing else.

``data_origin`` is ``"demo"`` for a seeded demonstration estate (the frontend
has to badge that honestly) and ``"live"`` otherwise. The per-component
breakdown, the drivers and the raw inputs stay internal: they are operational
detail about a private community.
PublicLivingScoreSummary.title: PublicLivingScoreSummary

PublicPhotoResponse.description: One photo of a public estate: the unguessable handle and its caption.
PublicPhotoResponse.title: PublicPhotoResponse

RegisterRequest.description: Public registration creates residents; trusted roles are operator provisioned.
RegisterRequest.title: RegisterRequest

ResidencyRequestCreate.description: A resident's request to be admitted to one unit of one estate.
ResidencyRequestCreate.title: ResidencyRequestCreate

ResidencyRequestReject.description: The optional reason an administrator declining a request may record.
ResidencyRequestReject.title: ResidencyRequestReject

ResidencyRequestResponse.description: One residency request, as the admin queue or the resident's own list shows it.
ResidencyRequestResponse.title: ResidencyRequestResponse

ResidencyRequestStatus.description:
The lifecycle of a resident's request to join an estate.

A request is created ``pending`` by the resident and is only ever moved to
``approved`` or ``rejected`` by an estate administrator of the *same* estate.
The three values are the database check constraint and the API vocabulary; a
new state is a migration, never a string typed at a call site.
ResidencyRequestStatus.title: ResidencyRequestStatus

TriageDecisionRequest.description:
An HOA admin's decision on one suggestion.

``accepted`` copies the suggestion; ``overridden`` supplies at least one
corrected label; ``dismissed`` supplies none. Which combination is legal is
decided by the service, because only it knows the suggestion being decided.
TriageDecisionRequest.title: TriageDecisionRequest

TriageSuggestionResponse.description: One stored suggestion and its (write-once) decision.
TriageSuggestionResponse.title: TriageSuggestionResponse

Return the estates this user has a persisted membership in.

The estate is the tenant boundary, so the frontend must let the user pick
from this server-resolved list rather than typing an ``estate_id``. An empty
list means the user is registered but not yet provisioned by an HOA.

Every attempt is recorded for security monitoring and a per-account
failure window is enforced before credentials are verified.

Ask for the triage suggestion for one complaint.

Idempotent: the first call asks the AI layer and stores exactly one
suggestion; later calls return the stored row without another provider call.
Accept, override or dismiss the suggestion. Write-once.

The work order raised for this complaint.

Read by the complaint's author (so they can see progress without being able
to list the estate's work) or by an HOA admin of the estate. The DTO is the
existing work-order response, unchanged.
The estate's photos in display order. Any member of the estate may read.

Upload one photo, re-encoded and stored server-side under a random id.

The bytes are read with a hard ceiling (never the whole file into memory
first), then decoded, capped and re-encoded by the service. The uploaded
filename is ignored.

get.description: Return the estate's active join code, or 404 when there is none.
List this estate's members, newest first.

post.description:
Join the estate your code belongs to, against your unit number.

No approval step: the code and the unit number are the whole proof. A
mistyped or unusable code is a uniform 404, and five of them in fifteen
minutes is a 429.

Add an already-registered service provider to this estate, by email.

The service owns the one commit (membership + ``joined`` event) and answers a
single uniform 404 for every email that is not a registered provider, 409
when they are already a member, and 429 after five failed lookups.

Create up to 500 units in one estate, all or nothing.

The estate is required as a query parameter and the caller must be an
``hoa_admin`` *member* of it. ``complex_name`` and ``suburb`` come from the
estate, never from the body.

get.description: Fetch a single property by id.
Read the legacy property score only inside an authorized estate scope.

The estate's provider directory: only providers who are members of it.

``estate_id`` is required and is authorized against a persisted
``hoa_admin`` membership inside the service, so a client-supplied estate is
never proof of access. Provider phone numbers and email addresses appear in
this response and are shown here (and on ``/providers/me``) only.

Nothing is granted here: the request is recorded ``pending`` and the estate's
administrators are notified. A repeat submission while one is pending is a 409,
and repeated attempts against unknown units are rate-limited.
